insight: After 5 minutes, stop believing you must stay in your assigned lane. Your primary goal is farming creeps, and heroes (both enemy and allied) are the main limiting factor to farm. Relocate to empty lanes or jungle to maximize farm without hero interference.

source.title: The Myth That Ruins Your Farm

insight: Before teleporting back to lane after respawning, check the minimap for hero density. If your lane has multiple heroes and another lane is empty or will soon be empty, TP to that lane instead to avoid shared farm and unnecessary fights.

source.title: The Myth That Ruins Your Farm

insight: Minimize time spent around allied heroes to avoid sharing creeps. Prioritize jungling near a lane that will push into you in the near future (e.g., when enemy mid laner respawns and TPs to push) rather than staying in a contested lane.

source.title: The Myth That Ruins Your Farm

insight: Avoid taking fights that don't serve your farm goal. Wasting time in prolonged fights with minimal creep gain delays your core item timings far more than repositioning to a better farming location.

source.title: The Myth That Ruins Your Farm

insight: If all lanes have heroes and you can't safely farm, jungle behind or near your tower when enemy threats are visible elsewhere on the map. This prevents you from getting baited into unfavorable fights.

source.title: The Myth That Ruins Your Farm

insight: The 5-minute mark is when heroes typically have upgraded boots and jungle viable levels. After this point, midlaners should also think dynamically about rotating between lanes and jungle based on hero positioning.

source.title: The Myth That Ruins Your Farm

insight: Like carries and midlaners, offlane heroes past 5 minutes should abandon their lane if it's congested with heroes. Relocate to empty farm or jungle rather than forcing fights or sharing creeps with allies.
